To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business (!!)

Okay, deep breath. I have news, and I’m putting it here before Thanksgiving because if I have to announce it while passing the rolls at Ruthie’s, there is a very real chance I’ll just say “so anyway, lowercase llc” and hide in the kitchen.

Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business. My business. (!!)

I filed Fernhollow Photo LLC on October 22, the website went live November 1, and there are already fourteen weddings booked for 2027. I am excited, scared, proud, and occasionally all three before breakfast. Mostly excited. Or at least that’s what I’m telling myself while I sit very still and stare at my calendar.

Some of you know the work part of this already, but here’s the whole timeline. Marisol told me on October 6 that Rosebud Lane would be closing at the end of October. I shot for her for four years, and I loved being part of that studio. Rosebud Lane is where I learned how much work goes into photographing a wedding well, and also how many times you can kneel on a dance floor before your knees start sending you formal complaints.

I’m not going to try to tell Marisol’s side of things for her. What I can tell you is what this meant for me, and how much I owe her.

Marisol basically taught me everything. She trusted me with huge days in people’s lives, taught me how to do this work, and told me I was ready before I completely believed her. Six of those fourteen booked weddings came through referrals from her. That means an enormous amount to me. So, Marisol, if you read this: thank you. Again. Probably not for the last time.

The other eight couples found me on their own, which still makes my brain do a little error message when I think about it too long.

Dahlia and Ken were the first booking that was 100% mine. They’re getting married at Timberline on June 12, and they found me through the photos I took of Marisol’s couple at Multnomah Falls. So if you’ve ever heard me say “just one more” while standing dangerously close to a waterfall, apparently that was a business investment. They’re lovely, I’m ridiculously excited about their wedding, and seeing their deposit come through was one of those moments where something stopped being a maybe in my head.

That’s the part I really want everyone to understand: this is scary, but it isn’t reckless. I’ve been planning Fernhollow in my head for about two years. I didn’t wake up one morning, buy a camera strap with inspirational words on it, and quit everything on a whim.

Fourteen weddings are booked. Not fourteen people who might possibly inquire someday. Fourteen actual weddings on the calendar. June is the busiest month so far with four, and the furthest one from home is at Wallowa Lake in September. There are deposits in, there’s a real calendar, and Jae is going to second shoot the bigger weddings with me, paid per wedding. I’m not planning to do everything alone, and I’m also not planning to pay Jae in gratitude and leftover cake.

Although the cake was pretty good. More on that in a second.

Dad, this next paragraph is specifically for you. Please read it before warming up the health insurance speech.

Health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5, and my coverage starts January 1. An actual insurance plan, not “I’m young-ish and usually fine” or “Sam says positive thinking counts.” I knew that would be one of your first questions, and honestly, fair. You can still worry about me because you’re my dad and I think that’s in your contract, but you do not need to explain health insurance to me over the turkey. I love you. I handled it.

Filing the LLC was much less glamorous than business announcements make it sound. I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Then I cried a little, because apparently I am someone who cries in a Fred Meyer parking lot over government paperwork now. It was such a normal-looking moment for something that felt huge. No ribbon, no confetti, just me in the driver’s seat with my laptop, feeling like I had pushed a door open and could finally see the room on the other side.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW.

To be clear, the business is FERNHOLLOW. Two Ls. The cake had one L and unlimited good intentions. We ate it anyway, obviously, and it was delicious. I considered keeping the misspelling as a very exclusive budget brand, but Sam says no.

And Grandma, I need you to know where the name came from, because it’s for you.

Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham, where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I can still remember being on that trail, trying to make the camera do what I could see in my head. I did not know then that taking pictures would become my whole work life. I just knew that looking closely at things felt important, and that you let me try.

So every time I say the name of this business, that’s where I am for a second. On that trail, with your camera. Fernhollow sounded better than Fred Meyer Parking Lot Photo, but honestly both locations have played a role.

I don’t want anybody reading this and thinking I expect it to be easy. I know weddings are a lot. I know working for myself is a lot on top of that. There are absolutely nights when I look at everything and think, “Wow, Tessa, this was a choice you made with your entire chest.” But I also know I’m good at this work, I’ve been learning it for years, and couples are choosing me. Not just choosing the studio I work for. Choosing me.

That’s the part that makes me feel like crying again, in a good way. No Fred Meyer required.

I’m also not expecting everyone in the family to become an unpaid Fernhollow marketing department. I mostly want you to know what’s going on and be excited with me if you can. Questions are okay. Being a little nervous is okay. I’m a little nervous too. I just don’t want the only version of this story to be “Tessa is doing something risky,” because there’s so much more to it than that.

And since this is going on the family blog, there is one extremely important business matter left: does anyone want free family pictures at Thanksgiving?

I’ll be at Ruthie’s with Sam, the rolls, the cranberry thing, and my camera. If you want an updated family picture, a picture of you and your kids, a couple photo, or individual proof that you own something other than a hiking fleece, speak up. Free. No sitting fee, no holiday mini-session nonsense. We can do it before dinner so nobody has gravy on their shirt, or after dinner if gravy on your shirt is part of your personal brand.

Uncle Greg, you can be holding a fish if you really want, but you’ll have to supply the fish.

Okay. That’s the news. Fernhollow Photo is real, I’m building it carefully, and I’m really proud of it. Thank you for listening to me practice saying all of this out loud. See you at Thanksgiving, where I will be taking zero questions during the actual cutting of the turkey and approximately one million pictures afterward.

Love you all. Wish me luck. And maybe spell-check any cakes.
